question: Answer in short bullet points, "unknown" if unsure. (1) CAPTIONS: font style, size relative to frame, vertical position, words per screen, case, outline; which words (if any) get a different colour or size and WHY (the number, the conflict word, a name, or random); does any caption pop or animate in? (2) FIRST 2 SECONDS: what is on screen in frame 1, what is the first spoken line, is there movement, is text on screen. (3) VOICE: pace (fast/medium/slow), pauses between sentences, emphasis changes. (4) SFX: list each sound effect type (whoosh, hit, riser, pop...) and approximately when. (5) MUSIC: genre, volume vs voice, any drop before the payoff. (6) VISUAL DEVICES: zoom/punch-ins, speed ramps, freeze frames, circles/arrows, split screens; how many cuts per 10 seconds. (7) LAST 2 SECONDS: what happens and does it loop to the start.
answer:
**(1) Captions**
- Style: Heavy bold sans-serif (all caps), white text with black outline.
- Size/Position: Medium size, centered vertically (middle of screen).
- Words per screen: 1-3 words flashing rapidly.
- Colour/Size: No words get special colour or size.
- Animation: Words pop in sequentially to match the speech rhythm.

**(2) First 2 Seconds**
- Frame 1: A basketball arena floor with a scoreboard in the background and a man in black athletic wear holding a floor mop.
- First spoken line: "This guy was just wiping the court when a basketball..."
- Movement: The man is wiping the floor, walks slightly, and a basketball rolls into view.
- Text: The words "THIS GUY WAS" appear on screen immediately.

**(3) Voice**
- Pace: Fast, engaging storytelling pace.
- Pauses: Minimal to maintain high engagement.
- Emphasis: Strong emphasis on action words ("wiping", "surprised", "hidden talent", "dunks").

**(4) SFX**
- None (reliance on voiceover and crowd noise in video).

**(5) Music**
- Genre: Upbeat, energetic instrumental background track.
- Volume: Lower than voiceover, clear.

**(6) Visual Devices**
- Cuts: Fast-paced editing, approximately 3-4 cuts per 10 seconds.
- Zoom/Punch-ins: Punch-ins used when he jumps to dunk.
- Speed ramps: Slow-mo applied during the dunk sequence.

**(7) Last 2 Seconds**
- Action: The basketball bounces away after the dunk as the man turns away.
- Loop: Does not seamlessly loop back to the start.
